subject: stinging tree
title: Touch This Tree Once and It Can Hurt for Months

scenes.text: Touch this tree once and it can hurt for months.
It's the gympie-gympie, a stinging tree from the rainforests of eastern Australia, with broad, soft-looking leaves.
That fuzz is a coat of tiny needles. Each one injects venom, like a hypodermic.
It feels like fire, then hours of pain. Long afterward, even a shower can bring it back.
In 2020, Queensland scientists found why: a toxin shaped like those in spider and cone snail venom.
It seems to change the pain nerves themselves. A plant, armed like a spider.

description:
Brush against an Australian stinging tree and the pain can last for days, weeks or even months.
The gympie-gympie and its relatives (genus Dendrocnide) grow in the rainforests of eastern Australia. Their leaves are covered in fine hairs that work like hypodermic needles. Victims describe a burning pain that eases over hours, followed by days or longer in which even taking a shower can reignite it. In 2020, a University of Queensland team led by Irina Vetter reported in Science Advances that the hairs carry a previously unknown family of small proteins, named gympietides, with a structure like spider and cone snail toxins. They act on sodium channels in pain-sensing nerve cells, which may explain why the pain lasts so long.
Would you walk through that forest? Comment below.
first_comment: One researcher described the sting as being burnt with hot acid and electrocuted at the same time. Would you walk through that forest?
